solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Skirt with narrow opening ignored by a model (9)

indicatorNotes.ignored: to ignore something is to pass over it, so the letters for 'by' are left out of the opening

blocks.note: a mini is a short skirt
APERTURE (a narrow opening) with PER (by, as in 'per hour') taken out

annotation.surface: A fashion model in a skirt with a slit that nobody seems to notice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'By' looks like it joins the clue together, but it is the thing ignored: PER means by. 'A model' is the definition, not part of the skirt story.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain noun synonym: a small-scale replica of a ship or building is both a model and a miniature.

entries.clue: Leader with magic touch, misunderstood at first, is winning promotion after promotion (5)

indicatorNotes.at first: at first points to the opening letter only
indicatorNotes.winning: to win something is to take it in, so IS holds the promotion
indicatorNotes.after promotion: something promoted goes up, and in a down clue AD read upwards becomes DA

blocks.note: first letter of misunderstood
the word itself
an ad promotes a product

annotation.surface: A boss with a golden touch rising through the ranks despite being misunderstood.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Promotion' appears twice with different jobs: first an advert, then the instruction to raise it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by story: the legendary king of Phrygia turned everything he touched to gold.

entries.clue: Like weapons of mass destruction: in doubt once UN turns up (7)

indicatorNotes.once UN turns up: in a down clue, turning up reads letters upward, so the UN in the word flips

blocks.note: uncertain; its first two letters are the pair to flip

annotation.surface: Uncertainty over weapons of mass destruction, once United Nations inspectors arrive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'UN turns up' reads as the United Nations arriving, but it is two letters of the word for 'in doubt' being reversed.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: atomic bombs are the defining weapons of mass destruction, so such weapons are typically of this kind.

entries.clue: Fearful article covering strain between west and east (3-8)

indicatorNotes.covering: a cover goes over the outside, so AN wraps round everything else
indicatorNotes.between: between puts the strain in the middle, after WEST and before E

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
the word itself
to rick is to strain or sprain, as in a ricked neck
E = east

annotation.surface: A nervous article about the tensions between the Western and Eastern blocs.
annotation.walkthrough: West is used whole while east is only E, which is easy to miss.
annotation.definitionFit: A near-synonym: being struck with awe mixes wonder with fear, so the state is fearful.

entries.clue: Dangerous [and] nefarious leaving Rio in chaos (6)

indicatorNotes.leaving: when someone leaves a place they are no longer in it, so the city's letters come out of the word
indicatorNotes.in chaos: chaos is disorder, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the word to be reduced
these letters are taken out, leaving NEFAUS to be rearranged

annotation.surface: A villain escaping Rio de Janeiro amid the chaos.
annotation.walkthrough: Rio looks like the Brazilian city but is just three letters to strike out.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym by negation: what is not safe carries risk, which is what dangerous means.

entries.clue: Unnatural ability originally rattled providers of Fuel drink (8)

indicatorNotes.originally: originally means at the origin, so take only the word's first letter

blocks.note: extrasensory perception
first letter of rattled
Esso is an oil company brand

annotation.surface: A psychic shaken by the fuel company, reaching for a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fuel drink' reads as an energy drink; split it, and the fuel providers are a petrol brand.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: this strong black Italian coffee is one kind of drink.

entries.clue: Christian celebration rejected by American state (5)

indicatorNotes.rejected: something rejected is sent back, so the celebration is written backwards

blocks.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American
the Mass, the Eucharist; reversed to SSAM

annotation.surface: A church service turned away by one of the American states.
annotation.walkthrough: 'American state' reads as one phrase, but American is only A, and the state is in India, not the USA.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: Assam is one of the states of north-east India, best known for its tea.

entries.clue: Previously advanced onto Monopoly square (3)

indicatorNotes.onto: in a down clue, putting one thing onto another sets it above, so A comes first

blocks.note: A = advanced, as in A level
GO is the starting square on the Monopoly board

annotation.surface: A board-game move: advance to a Monopoly square.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Advance to Go' is a famous Monopoly card, which makes the surface sound like a game instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: An adverb synonym: 'long ago' and 'previously' both place an event in the past.

entries.clue: Australian mangetout of the moment quietly added into main (4,3)

indicatorNotes.added into: adding something into a thing puts it inside, so the pieces go inside the main

blocks.note: now = current, of the moment
P = piano, quietly in music
the main is an old word for the open sea

annotation.surface: A trendy Australian vegetable quietly slipped into the main course.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Main' suggests the main course, but it is the ocean. Mangetout is a flat edible-podded pea.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional name: Australians and Americans use this name for what Britons call mangetout.

entries.clue: Drake maybe covering page upon page [in] Canadian flag (5,4)

indicatorNotes.covering: a cover goes round what it covers, so the male wraps around P
indicatorNotes.upon: in a down clue, upon means sitting on top, so the first part stands above the second page

blocks.note: a drake is a male duck
P = page
a leaf of a book is a page

annotation.surface: Sir Francis Drake draped over page after page of a Canadian flag.
annotation.walkthrough: Drake reads as the explorer or the rapper, but it is a duck. 'Page' gives two different things.
annotation.definitionFit: A metonym: the red leaf in the centre of Canada's flag names the flag itself.

entries.clue: Devil retreats with feeling of disgust in possession (7)

indicatorNotes.in possession: whatever is in possession of something holds it, so the retreats hold the disgust inside them

blocks.note: dens are private retreats
'ick!' is a cry of disgust

annotation.surface: The Devil backing away in revulsion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retreats' looks like a verb for the devil, but it is a plural noun. 'What the dickens?' is an old oath.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'the dickens' is an old euphemism used in oaths in place of the devil.

entries.clue: Soup lid covering nothing — you might snap at this! (5,2)

indicatorNotes.covering: a lid covers what is under it, so TOP goes round the nothing

blocks.note: pho is a Vietnamese noodle soup
a top is a lid
O looks like zero

annotation.surface: A cook growling at a pot lid with nothing under it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Snap' suggests a bad temper, but here it means taking a photograph.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint: a photo opportunity is an event staged so photographers can snap pictures.

entries.clue: Take action against publication erasing lives (3)

indicatorNotes.erasing: to erase is to rub out, so the letters meaning 'lives' are removed from the publication

blocks.note: an issue of a magazine
lives = exists = is; these letters are removed

annotation.surface: Suing a magazine that wiped people out of its pages.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lives' looks like the plural of life, but it is the verb: he lives, he is.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal sense: 'take action against' is court language, and bringing a lawsuit is exactly that.

entries.clue: Peel off tape to cook sweet treat (6-5)

indicatorNotes.to cook: to cook the books is to doctor them, so cooking the letters rearranges them

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: Kitchen instructions: strip off the tape before making a dessert.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a recipe step, and the treat itself is a recipe, which hides the fact that the first three words are just letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: an apple on a stick dipped in hard toffee is a fairground sweet.

entries.clue: Everyday media, unusually, bother enlightening school? (1,4,1,5)

indicatorNotes.unusually: done unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters take an unusual order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 5 letters
ado = fuss, bother
the school of Buddhism aimed at enlightenment

annotation.surface: Wondering whether the daily media bother to educate a school.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Enlightening school' looks like any school teaching pupils; the question mark signals a religious school of thought.
annotation.definitionFit: An American idiom: things so common they sell twelve for ten cents are ordinary, everyday.

entries.clue: Fish tongue ultimately lacking strong ingredient (6)

indicatorNotes.ultimately lacking: ultimately means at the end, so the word lacks its final letter

blocks.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
LICK (to tongue) without its last letter

annotation.surface: A fish dish whose sauce is short on punch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' is the verb, to lick, not the organ or a language.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: the bulb is famous for its pungent, strong flavour in cooking.

entries.clue: Bible reader[’s] acceptable idea about exorcism? (9)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so GOER goes around the spell

blocks.note: a goer is a proposal that can go ahead
an exorcism is a kind of spell; the question mark flags the example

annotation.surface: A preacher considering an exorcism.
annotation.walkthrough: Goer in this sense is British: a plan that is a goer is viable.
annotation.definitionFit: A church role: the person who reads the Gospel passage aloud at a service reads from the Bible.

entries.clue: Unopened finest china keeping current value (8)

indicatorNotes.Unopened: something unopened has not had its front broken into, so the word loses its first letter
indicatorNotes.keeping: to keep something is to hold it, so the pieces hold the current inside

blocks.note: BEST without its first letter
I is the symbol for electric current
china plate = mate in Cockney rhyming slang, so china = friend

annotation.surface: An antiques dealer valuing a fine set of china still in its box.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all porcelain, which hides the rhyming slang; Cockney rhyming slang swaps a word for a phrase that rhymes with it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to value a house or a painting is to put a price estimate on it.

entries.clue: Inverted winger ran [and] took the ball forward? (8)

indicatorNotes.Inverted: inverted means turned upside down, so in a down clue the winger reads upwards

blocks.note: a bird has wings
colours ran = bled

annotation.surface: A football report: the inverted winger ran with the ball.
annotation.walkthrough: An inverted winger is a real football position, which makes the surface convincing; here the winger flies, and 'ran' is what dye does in the wash.
annotation.definitionFit: A sporting sense: moving the ball upfield with small touches of the foot is dribbling.

entries.clue: Perhaps Sun King regularly stripped hearts bare (8)

indicatorNotes.Perhaps: perhaps flags an example: the Sun is one kind of star
indicatorNotes.regularly stripped: stripping at regular intervals removes every other letter

blocks.note: the Sun is a star
K = king in chess
the alternate letters of hEaRtS

annotation.surface: Louis XIV, the Sun King, baring his heart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sun King' reads as Louis XIV and must be split. 'Stripped' hints at nakedness but is doing letter work.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang: starkers means stark naked, so completely bare.

entries.clue: A very loud Mediterranean island turned warm (7)

indicatorNotes.turned: something turned faces the other way, so the island reads backwards

blocks.note: the article itself
ff = fortissimo in music
Elba, Napoleon's island of exile

annotation.surface: A noisy Mediterranean island that has warmed up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Warm' looks like the weather of the island, but it describes a friendly person.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym for manner: a warm person is friendly and easy to talk to.

entries.clue: Fail to justify force[’s] conviction (6)

blocks.note: results that belie hopes fail to justify them
F is the symbol for force in physics

annotation.surface: A court verdict that the use of force could not justify.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Conviction' suggests a guilty verdict, but it means a firmly held view.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the non-legal sense: a conviction is something you are firmly persuaded of.

entries.clue: How friend may introduce herself [in] Islamic territory (7)

blocks.note: surface padding: it turns the wordplay into a question of what she would say
an introduction starts 'I'm a…'
mate = friend, and what she says she is

annotation.surface: A friend introducing herself in Islamic lands.
annotation.walkthrough: The friend's self-introduction, I'M A MATE, run together spells the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A word-formation: the -ate suffix marks a ruler's domain, so the land an imam governs.

entries.clue: Big beasts in position (6)

blocks.note: in = fashionable = hip
POS is an abbreviation for position

annotation.surface: Large animals in their places.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as a linking preposition but is the adjective, fashionable.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the hippopotamus is one of the heaviest land animals.

entries.clue: Editor taking back tasteless, ignorant curse (3,3,5)

indicatorNotes.taking: the editor takes in, so holds, the next word inside ED
indicatorNotes.back: taking something back returns it the way it came, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: ED is short for editor
naff is British slang for tacky or tasteless
blind to something = ignorant of it

annotation.surface: A newspaper editor swearing at crass, uninformed writing.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase is British slang built from 'effing' and 'blinding', two mild swear words; it is a verb, like 'curse' here.
annotation.definitionFit: A British idiom: to eff and blind is to swear a stream of oaths, so to curse.

entries.clue: Cover for priest arrested by Special Branch (3)

indicatorNotes.arrested by: someone arrested is held, so the answer is held inside the words that follow

blocks.note: speciAL Branch

annotation.surface: A priest taken into custody by the police's Special Branch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cover' looks like a disguise for an undercover priest, but it is a garment. Special Branch is the British police unit for national security.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the alb is the long white vestment covering a priest at Mass.

entries.clue: Business class initially ejected French composer (5)

indicatorNotes.initially ejected: initially means at the start, so the first letter is thrown out

blocks.note: biz is informal for business
SET (a class) without its first letter

annotation.surface: A composer thrown out of business class.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Business class' reads as the airline cabin and must be split.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the writer of the opera Carmen was a nineteenth-century Frenchman.

entries.clue: Free time visiting Wild Bill (7)

indicatorNotes.visiting: a visitor goes inside someone's home, so the time goes inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.Wild: something wild is out of control, so the letters of the name run in a new order

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
anagram fodder, 4 letters, rearranged around the time

annotation.surface: Spending your free time visiting Wild Bill Hickok.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wild Bill' reads as the Western gunfighter Hickok, but 'wild' is only an instruction and 'Bill' just four letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: liberal means free, as in generous with money or unrestricted in views.

entries.clue: Charles who performed [in] Shaft (3)

blocks.note: the American soul singer and pianist, whose surname is the answer
a shaft of light or sunshine

annotation.surface: Ray Charles appearing in the film Shaft.
annotation.walkthrough: Shaft looks like the 1971 detective film, but it is a beam of light.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: Ray Charles's surname, and a narrow beam, as a shaft of sunlight is a ray.

entries.clue: Eye copies of Zulu retaining a stylish energy (7)

indicatorNotes.retaining: to retain is to keep hold of, so the copies hold the A inside them

blocks.note: a private eye is a PI
Zulu is Z in the NATO alphabet; several copies
the article itself

annotation.surface: An eye looking over reproductions of Zulu art.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eye' is a detective, not the organ. The number of Zs is not stated, only 'copies', so the enumeration settles it.
annotation.definitionFit: A two-part description: pizzazz combines flair (stylish) with zip and vigour (energy).

entries.clue: Thin and weak, like Oliver at the cinema? (5)

blocks.note: Oliver Reed, the British film actor
the suffix -y means 'like', as in stony or leafy

annotation.surface: A scrawny Oliver Twist on the film screen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Oliver' points to Dickens's Oliver Twist, but the cinema Oliver is the actor, and adding -Y makes 'like him'.
annotation.definitionFit: A description by likeness: a reed is a thin, fragile stalk, so a reedy voice or figure is thin and weak.

entries.clue: Female inside criminal court [is] clean (9)

indicatorNotes.inside: inside places F within the other letters
indicatorNotes.criminal: criminal means breaking the rules, so the letters break their order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters, which also tells you to put F in it
F = female
CT is the abbreviation for court

annotation.surface: A woman in a criminal court.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inside' works twice: it places the F and it is itself the fodder for 'criminal'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym, narrowed: to disinfect is to clean something of germs.
